In addition, the HKMA has implemented a print management system that requires employees to log in to printers to confirm each print request, thereby helping to reduce unnecessary printing and toner consumption. If printing is indeed necessary, double-sided printing and the use of black-and-white output are encouraged. The HKMA is also preparing to implement an internal electronic record-keeping system. Total paper consumption in 2022 was 20.5 metric tonnes (0.0114 metric tonnes per person), representing a 65.3% decrease from 2015 (Figure A). Figure A: Paper Usage Density The Financial Secretary's Office continues to adhere to the "4R" principle in its waste management practices. In addition to conventional waste, the HKMA has also reduced electronic waste by adopting technical solutions such as server virtualization and private cloud infrastructure. In 2022, the HKMA engaged an external firm for the first time to conduct a waste audit, analyzing the composition of waste generated by its offices. The audit found that food waste accounts for a significant portion of total waste, prompting the HKMA to launch a food waste recycling initiative (see page 41, "Strengthening Waste Management"). The total amount of non-hazardous waste generated in 2022, including general and recyclable waste, was 242.0 tonnes (0.135 tonnes per capita), representing a 4.8% decrease from 2015 levels (Figure 3). The volatility in trends was primarily attributable to work-from-home arrangements implemented during the peak of the coronavirus pandemic and the subsequent resumption of office operations following the fifth wave of the epidemic. Figure 3: Density of non-hazardous waste The Hong Kong Monetary Authority prioritizes waste reduction at the source and is committed to reducing, reusing, and recycling waste. In 2022, the HKMA engaged a company for the first time to conduct a waste audit, aiming to gain a clearer understanding of the composition of waste generated in daily operations (including plastics, paper, metals, glass, wood, electronic products, etc.) and to provide waste reduction recommendations. Based on the findings of this audit, the Monetary Authority launched a kitchen waste recycling program in November, installing kitchen waste collection bins in all pantry areas. Daily food waste is transported to an organic resource recovery center in Hong Kong, where it is converted into renewable energy for power generation. The residues generated during the conversion process can also be composted and used for landscaping and agricultural production. In addition, recycling bins are available at various locations throughout the office for convenient use. The HKMA shared recycling tips with staff and placed greater emphasis on improving the source separation of recyclables, as well as on the proper handling of items such as cardboard boxes, food containers, and beverage bottles. In addition, we continue to organize activities to enhance employees' environmental awareness, explain waste management policies, and encourage the effective use of office recycling facilities. Daily collected kitchen waste is transported to the Organic Resource Recovery Centre for plastic recycling. The HKMA operates two data centres (one active and one standby). As these two categories constitute the primary share of the institution's overall energy consumption, the HKMA has implemented green design measures and various energy-saving initiatives, including cabinet-type air-conditioning systems, LED lighting, and 24-hour monitoring of electricity efficiency. Following the completion of the aforementioned advisory study on green performance of data centers in 2022, the HKMA is preparing to implement recommendations aimed at enhancing overall energy efficiency. Preparations have also commenced to obtain certification for a green data center. The Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAH) recognizes the importance of fostering a culture of sustainable development. Accordingly, it regularly launches various initiatives and activities to educate and encourage staff to cultivate habits conducive to sustainability and to adopt green and digital working practices. The Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAHK) shared green living tips with its staff and provided the office's annual statistics on energy consumption and paper usage to remind them of the importance of addressing environmental issues at the individual level. It also encouraged staff to submit suggestions on sustainability matters. Under the leadership of a Senior Manager in the Administration Division, the task force brought together staff from various departments to brainstorm ideas and propose concrete measures for advancing a green workplace. Panel members also serve as ambassadors when introducing new green initiatives. The Monetary Authority encourages the wider community to adopt more environmentally friendly operational practices and has introduced a range of measures to enhance the efficiency of its own operations, the financial sector, and the broader economy, while minimizing resource consumption. The HKMA's Electronic Submission of Statistical Returns (STET) is a one-stop platform enabling banks to submit documents electronically to the HKMA, covering all types of periodic returns required on a weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annual basis. Another "e-Delivery" system serves as a secure electronic communication channel through which the HKMA disseminates notices, guidelines, and other information to banks. Both systems help save a substantial amount of paper annually. In handling bank complaints and enforcement matters, the HKMA has implemented measures to support the paperless submission of documents, enabling bank customers to lodge complaints via electronic channels and online forms. The HKMA is also developing a next-generation management information system to facilitate complaint handling and the transition from paper records to digital records. To reduce paper usage, the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) has adopted digital signatures in its day-to-day communications with participants, including the issuance of notices, account opening and termination letters, and responses to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, the CMU will continue to explore additional green initiatives, including the adoption of automated electronic systems for both internal and external communications. The HKMA promotes the adoption of electronic payment methods over cash and physical cheques by encouraging the public to use the Faster Payment System (FPS) and stored-value payment instruments. Further information on "Faster Payment System" (FPS) and stored value facilities is provided in the chapter "Hong Kong's Role as an International Financial Centre" of the HKMA's 2022 Annual Report. Distributing digital red envelopes is simple and convenient, helps reduce the use of physical red packets and cash, and contributes to advancing Hong Kong's sustainable development. To this end, the HKMA continues to actively promote through various social and traditional platforms, encouraging residents to distribute electronic red packets via Faster Payment System (FPS) or other e-wallet services using online or mobile banking during the Lunar New Year. Major banks and e-wallet operators have also launched various initiatives to encourage the use of e-red packets, such as providing user interfaces with a festive Chinese New Year atmosphere, enhancing functionality to improve convenience, and introducing lucky draws or cashback promotions. The HKMA is promoting electronic red envelopes on social media. For residents who still choose to distribute physical red envelopes during the Lunar New Year, the HKMA continues to encourage the use of "new-old" notes—notes that are older in circulation but in pristine condition—for stuffing into red envelopes. The introduction of new polymer notes reduces the need to print new banknotes, thereby lessening their environmental impact. Feedback from note-issuing banks indicates that the public has become increasingly accepting of the new banknotes in recent years. The Coin Collection Scheme reflects the efforts of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in promoting coin recycling. Coins collected through this program will be returned to circulation to meet public demand, enhance the efficiency of coin circulation, and reduce the need for minting new coins. The programme is equipped with two coin-counting vehicles. To date, it has served over one million users, collected more than 800 million coins, and processed a total face value of approximately HK$1.3 billion. In 2022, approximately 78% of users chose to allocate some or all of the value held in their accounts to top up their stored-value payment tool accounts. The Monetary Authority has maintained close collaboration with the Hong Kong Council of Social Service, deploying cash collection vehicles on Non-Governmental Organization flag-selling days to gather coins and thereby continue its support for social services. Launched in 2014, the Coin Collection Initiative, which utilizes mobile coin-counting vehicles, is the world's first systematic coin collection program based on the concept of mobile units. Over the years, it has received numerous local and international awards, with its innovative and environmentally friendly approach to coin processing widely recognized. The program features two coin collection vehicles, each equipped with two high-speed coin counting machines, to collect coins exchanged by the public. Members of the public may choose to exchange coins for banknotes, use them to add value to stored-value payment tools (such as Octopus cards or e-wallets), or donate them to the Community Chest as charitable contributions. In addition to coin collection, the cash van is also occasionally assigned to various educational activities, such as student visits.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) is conducting independent verification of the Climate Targets set by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA). The climate targets are established in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual ("SBTi Corporate Manual"). The purpose of this validation exercise is to verify whether the climate targets have been developed in reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. This verification exercise was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB). The verification procedures are designed to form an opinion and reach conclusions to provide a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process is conducted in accordance with the requirements set forth in the SBTi Corporate Standard. The HKMA is responsible for data collection and reporting. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. Based on the findings of this validation, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Council has provided reasonable assurance and concluded that: • The climate targets were established in reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. Xiao-Yin Shen, Audit Supervisor, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Council, 2023 March Verification Statement: The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Council has conducted an independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (the "HKMA") 2022 environmental data (the "2022 Data"). The 2022 data include total energy consumption for 2022, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emission intensity, paper consumption intensity, non-hazardous waste generation intensity and recycling rate, as well as the changes compared to 2015 levels. The HKMA's greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions data are compiled in accordance with the GHG Protocol, a joint initiative of the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD). The scope of verification covers data from January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2022, as well as data from January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2015, which were used for comparative annual performance analysis. The scope of verification covers assets at a total of six offices and warehouses: four offices located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Taikoo Place Phase I, and 4) Kowloon Trade Centre; and two warehouses located at 5) Leung Shun Industrial Centre and 6) Chong Lei Centre, situated in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan, respectively. The purpose of the validation is to provide reasonable assurance as to the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Authority examined representative data and supporting evidence selected from six assets. This verification exercise was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB). The verification procedures are designed to provide a reasonable level of assurance for forming opinions and conclusions. The verification process is conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The validation process tested data integrity and accuracy by tracing selected sample data back to their sources. It also reviewed the fundamental procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and conducted reliability tests. The verification process also included validating internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 data, and selecting representative data and information for audit checks. The underlying raw data and supporting evidence were also thoroughly reviewed during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for data collection and reporting. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Council verification team did not participate in the 2022 data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Council has provided reasonable assurance for the 2022 data and concluded: • The 2022 data are substantially accurate and reliable; • The overall data collection mechanism of the Monetary Authority is adequate. Shen Xiaoyin, Audit Supervisor, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Bureau, March 2023.

Expanding and accelerating climate action has become the most urgent priority of our time. Almost half of the critical decade to address the climate crisis has already passed. We need to reduce global carbon emissions by more than 40% over the next decade to have a realistic chance of limiting global warming to 1.5°C. However, greenhouse gas emissions have reached record highs. Latest climate science research indicates that the window for limiting global temperature rise to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels is rapidly closing. Everyone has clearly felt the impacts of a 1.1°C rise in global temperatures: record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe flooding, and storms are occurring with increasing frequency and severity across the globe. Hong Kong was no exception; after being battered by a ferocious super typhoon in September last year, it was subsequently hit by a century-scale rainstorm. Although we possess robust infrastructure and can respond rapidly to disasters, the impact remains severe, with widespread flooding, traffic disruptions, and damage to numerous road sections. All of these developments clearly underscore the urgent need for decisive and proactive climate action. Asia faces particularly significant challenges on its path to low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development with sustainability. We need credible transition strategies that appropriately balance climate action with economic growth and social inclusion. This is by no means an easy task. Due to rapid economic development and a fast-growing population in the region, its carbon emissions account for more than half of global total emissions. At the same time, the Asia-Pacific region, with its high population density and strategic geographic location, remains particularly vulnerable to rising sea levels and extreme weather events. Given the uneven pace of development among economies in the region, while the low-carbon transition may create new opportunities for some, it poses a significant challenge for others in mobilizing the necessary funding for the transition. Market estimates indicate that Asia-Pacific economies will require annual low-carbon transition investments exceeding USD 3 trillion over the next 30 years. As an international financial centre, Hong Kong has both the capacity and the responsibility to harness the power of finance to support low-carbon transition across Asia. As a banking regulator, market enabler, and responsible investor, the HKMA has made significant contributions to the sustainable development agenda. Readers will be able to gain insight into the various specific measures and initiatives launched by the HKMA over the past year from the various chapters of this report. In addition, to strengthen the internal governance framework of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and enhance the coordination of sustainable development efforts across different functional areas, we established the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee last year. For detailed information on the Oversight Committee, please refer to the newly added section on "Sustainable Governance." Hong Kong banks play a pivotal role in supporting Asia's transition to net-zero emissions. In addition to fulfilling our traditional role as a banking regulator and ensuring that banks properly manage climate risks in our day-to-day supervisory work, we also act as a facilitator, supporting the banking sector in providing financing for the transition to a low-carbon economy. One example is the development of a green classification framework to help banks and other financial institutions identify environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate goals. We launched the prototype of our Green Classification Framework for consultation in May and are currently refining the framework based on the feedback received during the consultation period. In addition, as stakeholders increasingly require higher-quality and globally comparable sustainability disclosure information, the HKMA is working with other regulators to establish a clear roadmap for Hong Kong, adopting the disclosure standards issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) in June, which constitute a comprehensive global baseline for sustainability reporting. As a facilitator, the HKMA's role extends beyond setting frameworks and rules; we are also committed to addressing pain points faced by the industry. Currently, many banks face limitations due to data constraints, making it difficult to conduct physical risk assessments. In light of this, the HKMA will launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform in the near term. Banks will be able to assess the impact of physical climate-related hazards on Hong Kong's residential and commercial buildings under various climate scenarios simply by entering property addresses, thereby helping banks manage associated climate risks. As a leading international financial centre in Asia and a hub for sustainable finance, Hong Kong has consistently played a bridging role in channeling international investment into Asia's sustainable development projects, supporting low-carbon transition in the region. In recent years, the total volume of international green and sustainable bonds arranged for issuance in Hong Kong has accounted for over one-third of the Asian market, significantly outpacing other regions. Of particular note is the fact that, for the third consecutive year and the second consecutive year respectively, the governments of Shenzhen and Hainan issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong in 2023, once again affirming Hong Kong's pivotal role as a green gateway connecting mainland China with the rest of the world. Hong Kong's sustainable bond activities have thrived, partly due to the demonstration effect of the Government Green Bond Programme. Since 2019, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds with a total value of approximately US$25 billion, subscribed to by both institutional and retail investors. We seize every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors, and distribution channels, thereby laying a foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance of the world's largest government retail green bond in 2022, we further issued the world's first tokenised government green bond in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the issuance of a second tranche of tokenised green bonds, denominated in four major currencies and issued in digital-native form, marking the world's first multi-currency digital green bonds. At the same time, we have proactively introduced a range of measures to enhance the vitality and competitiveness of Hong Kong's sustainable finance ecosystem. This encompasses work across multiple areas, including skills training, data enhancement, green fintech, and transition finance. In particular, in the area of talent development, we launched a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit under the Banking Professional Qualification Framework in 2023, providing systematic courses for banking practitioners to enhance their understanding and professional expertise in green and sustainable finance. Transition finance is another key focus of our work, providing funding for decarbonization activities in high-carbon and hard-to-abate sectors, thereby preventing these sectors from being unable to transition due to a lack of financial support. To support the robust development of transition finance, the HKMA will expand the local Green Taxonomy to cover transition activities. We will also expand the scope of the Green and Sustainable Finance Funding Scheme, which provides financial support to eligible bond issuers and borrowers, to include transition bonds and loans, thereby encouraging enterprises in the region to raise transition financing in Hong Kong. In addition, we will also strengthen communication and engagement with relevant stakeholders. Through public-private partnerships and blended finance models, we aim to attract private sector investment in sustainable development projects that have previously faced difficulties in securing financing. These efforts require cross-sector collaboration and are primarily coordinated by the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Coordination Group, co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional cooperation is equally important. In addition to our long-standing partnership with the International Finance Corporation (IFC) on the Green Banking Alliance, the Infrastructure Finance Promotion Office of the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) joined the Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Alliance and the Partnership on Green Development and Financing as founding members in 2023. Additionally, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero has announced plans to establish a branch in Hong Kong. Through these partnerships, we aim to promote skills training and knowledge sharing, thereby supporting the redirection of capital to sustainable projects both within the region and globally. To foster the development of new businesses and facilitate knowledge exchange, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority also assisted in hosting the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week earlier this year, attracting over 1,600 participants from nearly 30 regions, including top decision-makers from the global business and finance sectors. Together, they discussed strategies to expand regional climate financing and forged new partnerships. At the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum," the flagship event of Hong Kong Green Week, Chief Executive Mr. Yu Wai-man delivered a speech emphasizing that, as the manager of Hong Kong's official reserves and a major global asset owner, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority must lead by example as a responsible investor. Since 2015, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (HKMA) has led the development of green and sustainable asset investment, progressively expanding the Exchange Fund's portfolio of ESG and green assets in both public and private markets. In line with the Exchange Fund's portfolio goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050, the HKMA launched last year an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and expanded the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to another public market portfolio. Furthermore, green, social, and sustainable bonds that are prioritized for investment by the Monetary Authority have outperformed their investment benchmarks, underscoring the principle that doing good leads to financial success. In the private markets, we continue to pursue green-related investment opportunities and have become anchor investors in two Asia-focused transition investment funds. As of the end of 2022, the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio had decreased by 6% and 46% compared with the levels in 2021 and 2017, respectively, and remained below the overall market level. As a sustainable development institution, the HKMA will continue to advance by formulating its sustainability goals and plans on the foundation of the three pillars of environment, employees, and social responsibility. Specifically, the Monetary Authority strengthens our capacity to address climate change throughout the low-carbon transition journey by evaluating our environmental performance and implementing various internal measures. These measures cover emission reductions, energy efficiency improvements, and waste management, with the ultimate goal of fulfilling our commitment to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. We have established a plan to eliminate Scope 1 emissions entirely in the short term and have made significant progress toward our mid-term target of reducing Scope 2 emissions by 2030. To attract and retain top talent to effectively discharge the HKMA's key functions, the HKMA is committed to promoting the physical and mental well-being of its staff, alongside its green objectives. In addition, we have further collaborated with all stakeholders to promote financial inclusion, enhance the public's financial literacy, and raise awareness of fraud prevention, thereby contributing to the creation of a caring society. The climate challenge is immense and urgently pressing. Economies around the world are advancing toward a more sustainable future, a process expected to bring significant changes to financing activities and asset allocation. This transition entails significant risks, but it will also bring unprecedented opportunities. As a major global sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has a responsibility to take the lead in addressing these challenges. At the same time, we are also well-positioned to ride this momentum. The Monetary Authority of Hong Kong will fully support the industry in providing financing for the low-carbon transition. As a responsible investor and sustainable institution, we will lead by example and collaborate with like-minded partners to advance this critically important global agenda. President Edward Yiu Wai-man.

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are global in nature. The objectives of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) in its sustainable development work are to lead through its own policies and operations, ensuring that Hong Kong's financial system and the HKMA itself are resilient to climate change risks and support the transition to a more sustainable economy. By actively engaging with international and regional organizations, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAHK) is also committed to participating in the formulation of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at both the regional and global levels. As the banking regulator, the HKMA will further enhance banks' climate response capabilities and their ability to manage climate-related risks. Specifically, the key work items include: launching a new round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management practices and conducting a new round of consultation meetings as part of assessing banks' progress in implementing climate risk management regulatory requirements; continuing work to integrate climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review processes; completing the second round of industry-wide climate risk stress tests, providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process, and sharing key observations and lessons learned with the industry; strengthening sustainable development disclosures, including collaborating with local authorities to align relevant regulations with the International Sustainability Disclosure Standards (IFRS S1 and S2) as the global benchmark, and preparing for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's Third Pillar 1 framework on climate-related financial risks; and sharing guidance on best practices for transition planning with the industry. To foster the healthy development of banks in providing green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will continue to closely monitor local and international market and regulatory developments and maintain engagement with the industry to ensure that banks adopt appropriate sales practices. Furthermore, the HKMA will also play a facilitating role, committed to advancing the development of the green finance ecosystem and supporting banks in providing financing for economic transformation. We are soon to release our local green taxonomy and will continue to expand its coverage to include a broader range of activities, such as transition activities. At the same time, we will continue to explore the application of technological solutions to assist banks in identifying, measuring, and monitoring their climate risk exposures. One example is the upcoming cloud-based platform, which will facilitate banks' physical risk assessments. To enhance the professional competencies of our practitioners, we will also establish the Professional Level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit under the Banking Professional Qualifications Framework in 2024. Hong Kong is well-positioned to serve as a hub for sustainable finance both regionally and internationally. To fulfil this role, the HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing the recommendations set out in the 2023–24 Budget to expand the scope of the Government Green Bond Programme (GGBP) to cover sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of Hong Kong's green and sustainable bond market. At the same time, through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, the HKMA is attracting more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong. We will also continue to encourage more government bodies, institutions, and enterprises to raise green funds through Hong Kong, while exploring the potential synergies between green finance and technology. Furthermore, we will continue to assist in implementing the government-funded Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme to expand Hong Kong's talent pool in green finance. As Co-Chair of the Cross-Sectoral Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance (the Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other institutions and departments to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and initiatives aimed at advancing Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance development. In 2024, the Oversight Working Group will focus on three key areas: sustainability disclosure, the application of technology, and transition finance. As another key priority, the HKMA, in collaboration with the International Finance Corporation through the Green Banking Alliance, will continue to launch a series of targeted initiatives across Asia. These include conducting green finance research, providing insightful market analysis, delivering tailored professional training for banks, and issuing practical guidance to support financial institutions in establishing their own distinctive pathways for green transition. In 2024, we will also strive to deepen our collaboration with the Glasgow Net Zero Financial Alliance, the Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Alliance, and the Green Development Financing Partnership. As a responsible investor, the HKMA has committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund's investments through a responsible investment approach encompassing three pillars, ensuring portfolio resilience as we progress toward net zero. We fully recognize that achieving the objectives of the Paris Agreement requires a comprehensive economic transition. Accordingly, we are refining our net-zero strategy, with a focused emphasis on assets that deliver positive climate benefits to the real economy, while ensuring alignment with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. As an environmentally supportive institution, the Monetary Authority's decarbonisation strategy will continue to evolve in tandem with the latest developments in the market, regulation, technology, and other climate-related areas. To further strengthen the HKMA's climate response capabilities and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of leveraging technology solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our offices. Furthermore, we will continue to actively encourage our employees to participate in our sustainability initiatives, including launching awareness campaigns to foster sustainable habits and optimizing office processes and practices. Furthermore, the HKMA will continue to maintain a consistent, efficient, and sustainable procurement approach, including assessing suppliers' ESG practices during the selection and renewal of contracts. Building on the certification of green data centers achieved in 2023, the Monetary Authority has committed to adhering to the specified certification standards. Regarding the regular renewal of data center facilities, in addition to keeping pace with the latest technological advancements, we will also incorporate green design principles and operational practices. At the same time, we will continue to reduce e-waste through the application of technology and digital convergence, while actively modernising our internal systems to enhance efficiency and minimise potential risks as far as possible. Finally, in the realm of social priorities, the Monetary Authority will identify more community service opportunities for its staff, collaborate with the industry to promote financial inclusion and enhance financial literacy, and raise public awareness of fraud prevention.

Climate change impacts every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating these effects. Through its multiple roles as a central banking authority, banking regulator, market enabler, responsible investor, and sustainability institution, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong has contributed to advancing and accelerating Hong Kong's, and indeed the entire Asia region's, transition to net-zero emissions. The HKMA has established a robust governance framework for sustainable development, which leads the formulation of relevant strategies and policies, oversees the implementation of related measures, and ensures that the HKMA's own operations and working methods integrate sustainability considerations. To commit to sound corporate governance, the Monetary Authority has established a robust sustainable development governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency. The governance framework ensures that the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes effectively incorporate sustainability factors, and establishes robust mechanisms to monitor and evaluate the progress and effectiveness of sustainability initiatives. The HKMA's sustainable development governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its related sub-committees, which oversee the HKMA's work, including its efforts in sustainable development, and provide recommendations; the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, responsible for leading the HKMA's overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategy and policy at the management level; in the area of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office coordinates and oversees ESG-related activities within the Office; and for other functional areas, relevant task forces and working groups plan and implement sustainable development measures covering both banking and market development, as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Cross-Sectoral Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance, jointly established by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the efforts of various financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other relevant parties to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA's sustainability initiatives over the past few years, we established a Steering Committee in October as a new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA's various functional areas. Provide guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans for environmental, social, and governance (ESG) matters across the four functional areas of banking, market development, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations; oversee the implementation of ESG-related initiatives by the HKMA's various functional departments; evaluate the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and supervise its external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as ex officio members. Additionally, we will invite Executive Directors responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable development to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on their major achievements and future plans. The Steering Committee holds regular meetings, supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Division, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Affairs Department, and the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund. In addition to formulating and implementing their own sustainable development initiatives, the HKMA and the SFC jointly launched the Supervisory Group 2 in May 2020. The Steering Group, as a cross-agency platform, provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sector efforts within the financial industry to address climate and environmental risks, thereby consolidating Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For further details on the Supervisory Board's work, please refer to the chapter titled "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem."

Climate change represents a significant risk to the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has been committed to strengthening Hong Kong's financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face a range of sustainability and climate-related issues in their day-to-day operations. To continue fulfilling its vital role in the financial system and to channel more capital toward green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate-related risks. As the banking regulator, the HKMA has made special efforts to enhance banks' capacity to address and manage climate risks, while accelerating their work to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. The HKMA is committed to formulating various policy measures to enhance the banking sector's capacity to respond to climate risks. In August, the HKMA issued a notice on net-zero transition planning, setting out high-level principles to help banks maintain safety and soundness as the economy transitions to net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of that circular, we conducted a questionnaire survey among selected banks in the fourth quarter to understand their transformation planning measures. Based on the survey findings, we will share observations and best practices regarding transformation planning with the industry, and organize seminars or workshops to facilitate the exchange of experiences among industry practitioners. In the area of disclosure requirements, in response to the latest international developments—including the International Sustainability Standards Board's Sustainability Disclosure Standards released in June and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's (BCBS) November consultation on the third pillar disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks—the HKMA is strengthening its efforts to enhance the sustainability-related disclosure framework for Hong Kong's banks. Specifically, the HKMA is collaborating with relevant local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong to align with the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards. During the year, the HKMA strengthened its regulatory oversight of banks' climate risk management and provided them with guidance to further enhance their climate response capabilities and climate risk management practices. The HKMA has made significant progress in implementing its two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the bank regulatory framework. Climate risk management has now been incorporated as a standing agenda item in prudential supervisory meetings with bank management. Bank supervisors also employ an enhanced CAMEL rating framework, which incorporates climate risk factors, to assess banks' risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of the implementation of a two-year programme to incorporate climate risk factors into banking regulatory processes, the HKMA has revised its "green" assessment framework to focus on banks' transition planning measures. The HKMA is also reviewing the supervisory review procedures used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy levels and to determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, in order to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks in addressing climate-related risks. Under the two-year plan in 2023, a key priority was to commence, in the second quarter, a thematic review of climate-related risk governance following the conclusion of the 12-month implementation period for the "Climate Risk Management" module (GS-1) of the Supervisory Policy Manual. This review covers four key areas: governance frameworks for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategy, oversight of climate-related risk management, and institutional culture, awareness, and communication. The HKMA has implemented several improvements to its climate risk stress testing framework, including the introduction of a new five-year scenario to assess the potential impact on banks when economic and climate change shocks occur simultaneously. Following these enhancements and as part of the HKMA's ongoing regulator-led stress testing programme, the second round of climate risk stress tests commenced in June to comprehensively assess banks' climate risk exposures and further strengthen their capacity to manage climate-related risks. Forty-four banks participated in this stress test, representing an increase of over 60% compared to the initial pilot program in 2021. The HKMA also hosted a climate risk stress testing forum in November, with up to 300 banking professionals in attendance. By facilitating the exchange of experience among banks, the activity helps deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The HKMA also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review the progress made by banks in implementing the HKMA's Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) Module GS-1 on "Climate Risk Management". The HKMA held meetings with bank management to discuss their work on climate risk management and the shared challenges facing the industry, and reviewed information provided by the banks along with other public data to assess their progress. The HKMA has provided targeted guidance to banks, encouraging and supporting them to further strengthen their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA's regulatory expectations. As global attention to climate change intensifies and efforts to address the issue grow, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong has observed a rising demand for green and sustainable investment products, with some banks offering such products to meet customer needs. In light of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review on banks' sales of green and sustainable investment products and issued a circular in November setting out the standards expected of banks and sharing observed good practices. This notice covers multiple areas, including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training, and record-keeping. Its aim is to mitigate potential greenwashing risks and bolster investor confidence, thereby fostering the sound development of relevant investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can enhance data availability and risk analysis, thereby strengthening banks' capacity to manage climate-related risks. The HKMA will soon launch a pilot cloud platform to enable banks to assess the impact of physical climate risks on residential and commercial properties under various climate scenarios. Furthermore, the HKMA continues to collaborate with other central banks and regulatory authorities to explore how technological solutions can assist in conducting physical risk assessments. On the other hand, the HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable anti-money laundering (AML) practices by applying advanced analytics and artificial intelligence to reduce the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online shared data submission platform to fully automate the collection of financial crime risk data, thereby enhancing banks' operational processes for submitting anti-money laundering-related data in a sustainable manner. In September, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) held the "Green FinTech Competition" to seek solutions available to the market that would help the banking sector address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted over 85 submissions from approximately 70 companies. In December, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) hosted the Green and Sustainable Banking Seminar, providing a platform for the banking and technology sectors to explore the role of low-carbon technologies and green fintech in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and mainland China, while also announcing the results of the Green Fintech Competition. The event attracted approximately 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulatory bodies, and academia. To enhance transparency across financial markets and foster greater consistency in green and sustainable finance decisions, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), with the assistance of a consulting firm, has developed a local green taxonomy. In May, the HKMA published a consultation paper on the "Hong Kong Green Taxonomy Prototype," seeking stakeholders' views on the establishment and implementation of a green taxonomy. Based on the consultation outcomes, the HKMA is fine-tuning the framework prototype and identifying other areas for the next phase of framework development. The HKMA has engaged in the work of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), which has identified environmental crimes as predicate offenses for money laundering. Given the nexus between anti-money laundering and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations, this area is receiving increasing attention from regulators. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority recognises that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system; accordingly, it has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen current monitoring efforts. In its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, the HKMA takes climate change into account and incorporates analyses of climate-related risks into its various financial stability reports. By actively participating in the Scenario Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has helped further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to better understand the impacts of climate change on the macroeconomy and the financial system. As a member of the Transition Planning Task Force under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participated in analysing the interplay between transition planning by financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to adopt a forward-looking and dynamic perspective on climate-related financial risks. In terms of research, the HKMA has conducted multiple applied research projects exploring the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial sector and the economy. The research topics include the climate risk exposure of the banking sector and investment funds, ESG-driven capital flows, the impact of climate change on property prices, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance within global supply chains. The above research findings enhance the HKMA's understanding of the impacts of climate change and ESG issues on financial stability, thereby aiding the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, these studies will help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risks on financial stability. On the external front, the HKMA also disseminates research findings to a broad range of stakeholders through international activities on climate-related matters and various channels, including the HKMA Research Memorandum. The HKMA's Liquidity Arrangement Framework is a secured contingent funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The Monetary Authority has incorporated sustainability considerations into its assessment of eligible collateral under this framework, in line with NGFS recommendations. The Monetary Authority is actively engaging in international and regional discussions to address climate risks and advance the mainstreaming of sustainable finance. Through its engagement in this area, the HKMA has helped foster international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, while drawing on insights gained to strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading hub for green and sustainable finance in the region, the Monetary Authority is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and catalysts, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. This year, the HKMA has worked closely with local and international partners to build a richer ecosystem and promote further development of Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance. The Cross-Institutional Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance (Steering Group), jointly led by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the financial sector's response to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the Government's climate strategy. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Committee unveiled key measures to support Hong Kong in capitalizing on sustainable finance opportunities. The main areas of focus include sustainable disclosure, ecosystem strengthening, transition finance, and green fintech. Specifically, the Sustainability Disclosure Working Group has been established to formulate the roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. The roadmap will cover four key areas: sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills development. Additionally, a Transition Finance Working Group has been established to explore methods for supporting financial institutions and enterprises in their transition planning and reporting. The Supervisory Task Force also strengthened the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sector skills training and data enhancement. In particular regarding data, we continue to promote the adoption of the CDP Non-Listed Companies Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire 2, which was launched in collaboration with the Steering Group in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to closely monitor the latest developments in green and sustainable finance and enhance Hong Kong's position as a regional and global hub for green and sustainable finance. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new key initiatives to seize investment and financing opportunities arising from low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To support industry skills development, the Green and Sustainable Finance Centre, under the supervision of the Steering Group, has implemented the government's "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme," which provides funding to practitioners, students, and graduates who undergo training in green and sustainable finance and obtain relevant qualifications. As of December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training programmes or qualifications were registered as eligible under the Scheme, with over 560 subsidy applications approved. The HKMA has also launched the introductory level of a new module on "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the "Professional Qualifications Framework for the Banking Sector." This unit aims to promote talent development within the banking sector and enhance the overall professional capabilities of practitioners. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the banking sector to establish professional standards for the unit, addressing the rapidly growing demand for professionals in green and sustainable finance. To assist financial institutions and enterprises, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), in gaining a deeper understanding of key climate and sustainability issues—including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation, and transition planning—the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) collaborated this year with relevant government policy bureaus and departments, as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ), and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF), to organize a series of seminars and specialized workshops. These events attracted participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. On the student front, following the launch of the Sustainable Finance Internship Programme in 2022, training courses were held in January and February 2023 to enable interns and bachelor's degree graduates to deepen their understanding of sustainable finance. The HKMA recognizes the potential of technology in addressing climate-related data gaps and enhancing data quality. Accordingly, it is committed to making such data more accessible and improving their quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group launched a series of website optimization measures to provide financial institutions, enterprises, and the public with a one-stop portal for green and sustainable finance information. Key optimization projects include a sustainable disclosure e-platform, greenhouse gas emission calculation and estimation tools, as well as more centralized, user-friendly, and searchable data and resources. During Hong Kong Green Week, the Steering Group, in collaboration with Cyberport and the Investment Promotion Agency, co-hosted the "Leveraging Technology to Catalyze Sustainable Finance" event, showcasing leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong's strengths in green technology. The "Green Week in Hong Kong – Financial Theme" was held from 26 February to 1 March 2024. During the event, a series of sustainability-focused activities attracted over 1,600 participants from nearly 30 regions, including representatives from financial institutions, enterprises, central banks, international organizations, government agencies, academia, and consulting firms. The flagship event of "Green Week Hong Kong" is the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum," co-organized by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the International Finance Corporation. The forum brought together more than 400 distinguished guests, including top decision-makers from the global business and financial sectors, to discuss strategies for unlocking climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. This two-day event explored a broad range of topics, including the energy transition, decarbonization of heavy industry, the circular economy, the future of sustainable finance, and emerging climate technologies in Asia-Pacific emerging and developing markets. The forum has received a positive response from both the public and private sectors, with over 10 roundtable discussions, seminars, and other exchange activities co-hosted. The topics cover climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, financing for the transition to net zero, green finance taxonomies, and green development financing in the Belt and Road region. Furthermore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the International Monetary Fund co-hosted the "Asia Climate Finance Roundtable" on 29 February 2024 to discuss key measures for scaling up climate finance, as well as the roles of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. These activities form part of the HKMA's overall efforts to promote and enrich Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance ecosystem. They serve as a valuable platform for participants to advance new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address climate finance challenges in the Asia-Pacific region. The HKMA has also actively supported the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) launched the Green Banking Alliance⁵ as a collaborative platform to bring together financial institutions, banking industry associations, research bodies, and technology innovators within the region to advance the development of green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has held 22 training sessions and roundtable discussions, attracting over 7,300 participants from across the globe, including the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. In October, the Alliance, in collaboration with Crédit Agricole CIB, published a second cutting-edge research report titled "Developing Ambitious Green Banking Climate Strategies: Case Studies." The Alliance and Crédit Agricole CIB jointly published the前沿 issue research report "Developing Ambitious Green Banking Climate Strategies: Case Studies" in October. During the year, the Infrastructure Financing Promotion Office of the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong joined the newly established Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Alliance (CASI) and the Green Development Financing and Investment Partnership (GIFP) initiated by the International Alliance for Green Development under the Belt and Road Initiative. The collaboration with CASI and GIFP will help build capacity and facilitate knowledge sharing, while directing more capital toward green and sustainable projects across Asia and beyond. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of its Hong Kong branch, which will support net-zero transition efforts by financial institutions in both Hong Kong and mainland China. The HKMA assists the GFANZ in its work in an advisory capacity. To demonstrate the Government's resolve to address climate change, advance green finance, and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. The HKMA assists with the issuance of green bonds under the Programme. To date, the government has issued approximately USD 25 billion worth of green institutional and retail bonds. The proceeds have been allocated to more than 70 green government projects, including green buildings, waste management and recycling, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. To enhance transparency and accountability, the government publishes an annual Green Bond Report detailing the allocation of proceeds raised from green bonds and their expected environmental benefits. In the 2023-24 fiscal year, the Government continued its regular issuance of green government bonds, issuing approximately US$6 billion worth of green bonds in June. This tri-currency issuance, comprising bonds of various tenors in US dollars, euros, and renminbi, attracted a diverse range of investors and elicited a highly enthusiastic subscription response, with total subscriptions amounting to nearly USD 30 billion. The issuance of Renminbi bonds increased from RMB10 billion in January to RMB15 billion, and a 10-year Renminbi bond was issued for the first time. These measures helped extend the government's Renminbi yield curve and further diversified the range of offshore Renminbi products. Global investors responded enthusiastically to the government's issuance of green bonds, reflecting their recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to advancing green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued the second tranche of green retail bonds with a total value of HK$20 billion, further promoting market development and advancing inclusive finance. This issuance offers the public a stable-return investment opportunity, enabling them to both participate in and benefit from Hong Kong's development in green finance.

As a significant global asset owner and manager, the Monetary Authority plays a pivotal role in advancing green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The HKMA has been a pioneer in responsible investing. Since 2015, the Monetary Authority has led efforts in green and sustainable asset investment, requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise ownership rights and integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors into the management of the Exchange Fund's investments. In line with the "capital preservation first, long-term growth" principle, the HKMA invests prudently, believing that giving full attention to environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and to set a 2050 Net Zero Emissions target for its portfolio, the HKMA is committed to advancing its responsible investment journey, with a strong emphasis on sustainability, particularly the urgent challenge of climate change. This effort aims to enhance the resilience of the Exchange Fund and to achieve improved risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA has played a role in building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem by collaborating with like-minded investors, regulators, and international organizations to develop industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment practices across the financial sector and central banking community. Through supervision and cooperation measures, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to fostering a future where finance and sustainable development advance in tandem. Figure 1: The Exchange Fund's journey toward responsible investing underscores that comprehensive and reliable ESG information is essential for integrating sustainability and planning a credible climate transition to achieve net-zero targets. To fulfill its commitment to the NGFS Glasgow Declaration and the Cross-Institutional Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance Strategy Plan, the HKMA has taken a leading role by preparing this chapter on the responsible investment of the Exchange Fund in line with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, has established a Responsible Investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund in the management of the Exchange Fund's investments. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA's approach to practising responsible investment while concurrently meeting the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks associated with Exchange Fund investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the Responsible Investment Framework and risk management guidelines and monitors their implementation through regular reporting by the Sustainable Investment Group of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office is chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer and is responsible for coordinating and monitoring all ESG-related activities of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. The motions and progress reports discussed by the ESG Committee at its quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Oversight Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAHK) and including the Chief Executive and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, convenes biannually to provide guidance on ESG policies and initiatives across various MAHK functions, including those of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, to advance the MAHK's overall ESG objectives. Figure 2: The Responsible Investment Governance Framework of the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund As illustrated in Figure 1, the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund launched its responsible investment journey in 2016, initially focusing on managing ESG risks that could impact the financial performance of the Exchange Fund. As sustainability evolves rapidly and has surpassed risk considerations to become a strategic priority for major institutions worldwide, the Exchange Fund Investment Office has reviewed its responsible investment approach. July 2023 marked another milestone with the establishment of a new Business Strategy Department within the Investment Management Office of the Exchange Fund, led by the Chief Strategy Officer. This department is responsible for coordinating and leading the strategic development of the Investment Management Office and incorporated the former Responsible Investment Task Force, previously under the Risk Management and Surveillance Department, now renamed the Sustainable Investment Team. This strategic shift reflects the HKMA's elevation of the focus on responsible investing from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing investment matters related to sustainable development. The Sustainable Investment Group works closely with different teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office to integrate ESG factors and assists senior management of the Investment Office in managing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across various investment portfolios. In public market investments, the Credit, Regulatory and Monitoring Committee, composed of senior personnel from the Investment Office, reviews the incorporation of ESG factors into credit risk models based on the Sustainable Investment Group's input. It further monitors the ESG status of fixed-income portfolios through regular reports from the Risk Management and Monitoring Department. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Team has participated in the selection, appointment, and oversight of external equity portfolio managers from an ESG perspective (see the section "Promoting Active Ownership" under "Risk Management" on page 40). Private Market Investment – The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive Officer of the Monetary Authority, will consider private market investments and the ESG-related assessments made by the Risk Management team for each investment proposal. The HKMA recognizes that the physical and transition risks of climate change, along with related opportunities, may affect the long-term performance and value of Exchange Fund investment portfolios. The 2023 Emissions Gap Report, published by the United Nations Environment Programme, warns that unless greenhouse gas emissions are further reduced worldwide, global average temperatures are projected to rise by 2.5 to 2.9°C above pre-industrial levels by 2030. The urgent need for more ambitious policies, technological innovation, or behavioral shifts to curb temperature rise could exacerbate transition risks, including asset write-downs or stranded asset impacts. At the same time, extreme weather events are becoming increasingly frequent and severe, also imposing additional physical risks on investment projects. The Monetary Authority believes that investing in a greener future aligns with the objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG considerations. The HKMA's establishment in 2022 of a target for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier further underscores its commitment to the global climate agenda. The Monetary Authority continues to strengthen its three-pronged approach, with a clear focus on decarbonisation and transition. The following sections will elaborate on the methodology in detail. Figure 3: The HKMA's three-pronged approach to responsible investing. In the journey toward net zero, the HKMA prefers proactive engagement rather than divestment or exclusion from its investable universe. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is critical to achieving the Exchange Fund's primary investment objective. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries may narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment returns and risk profiles. Through an inclusive approach, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) can seize opportunities to invest in enterprises undergoing transformation that possess advanced technology and strong corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including those in high-emission sectors. Second, addressing climate change requires the transformation of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding relevant investment projects or divesting is insufficient to address carbon emission issues. In contrast, the Monetary Authority has supported these sectors by injecting strategic capital and actively exercising its ownership rights, thereby driving them to adopt sustainable and low-carbon operational practices, which will generate beneficial transformations for both the jurisdiction and the global community. In response to market developments, the Monetary Authority is refining its net-zero investment strategy, pursuing transformation outcomes that align with the Exchange Fund's objectives and global net-zero goals through a comprehensive approach, while upholding its guiding principles of responsible investment. The Exchange Fund continues to pursue sustainable investment opportunities by integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, thereby facilitating the climate transition and enhancing the long-term resilience of its asset portfolio (Figure 4). The HKMA's responsible investment initiatives maintained strong momentum in 2023. In the public markets, the HKMA has launched a new actively managed global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, managed by an external investment manager, and has expanded the application of a customised low-carbon stock index to another asset portfolio also managed by an external investment manager. Furthermore, the strong performance of green, social, and sustainable bonds prioritized for investment by the Monetary Authority has surpassed investment benchmarks, demonstrating the concept of "doing well by doing good." On the private market front, the Monetary Authority is actively building a resilient long-term growth portfolio, capitalizing on investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic trends such as climate and energy transition. For instance, this year the HKMA invested in two Asia-focused transition funds, underscoring its commitment to addressing Asia's climate transition needs. The Monetary Authority is committed to becoming a sustainable institution, taking a multi-pronged approach to reduce its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the Monetary Authority also prioritizes the physical and mental well-being of its staff and upholds social responsibility, while striving to advance financial inclusion and enhance the public's financial literacy. As a responsible institution, the HKMA has set sustainable development goals under three pillars: environment, employees, and social responsibility. Established in October, the Green and Sustainable Finance Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, serves as the primary decision-making body for institutional sustainability initiatives. The predecessor of the Steering Committee was the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Committee, which was responsible for guiding the HKMA in formulating the vision, strategy, and policies on corporate sustainability and social responsibility. At the departmental level, the Assistant Managing Director (Corporate Development and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and submits regular progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Special Committee and the Volunteer Service Committee provide support to the organization in coordinating its sustainable development initiatives; the former serves as a platform for discussing how to create a green workplace and for generating ideas, while the latter aims to foster a culture of volunteer participation. The Monetary Authority has formulated a roadmap to guide its transformation. The focus is on implementing decarbonisation strategies in daily operations, including operating green buildings and data centres, promoting green mobility, adopting energy-saving measures, leveraging digital tools and more environmentally friendly operational practices, reducing waste, and fostering a sustainability culture. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) also plans to deploy carbon embedding tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and to employ carbon offset measures for emissions that are difficult to abate. In addition to the environmental commitments regarding its day-to-day operations, the HKMA continues to introduce more eco-friendly initiatives for the wider public, covering channels for banks to submit electronic documents and make contact, as well as electronic payment services and coin collection programs available to the general public. To strengthen and sustain its operational capacity, the HKMA has engaged a professional team, built a talent pool, and placed emphasis on the physical and mental well-being of its staff. In terms of corporate social responsibility, the HKMA encourages employees to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; in procurement, it considers selecting social enterprises; it promotes financial consumer education; and it collaborates with the banking sector to ensure that all members of society have fair access to basic banking services. The remainder of this chapter sets out in detail the aforementioned strategies. Under the HKMA's overarching institutional risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers potential risks and threats arising from climate change, among others, that the HKMA faces in its day-to-day operations. Physical impacts from climate change, such as more frequent extreme weather causing flooding or other damage, could affect the Office of the Financial Secretary's premises and impede staff commutes. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its continuity plans to respond to extreme weather conditions. The HKMA also conducts regular evacuation drills and exercises to activate contingency facilities, ensuring that staff are always ready to implement continuity measures. The office design also incorporates several measures to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the IMF's energy consumption, air travel, and waste disposal practices. The HKMA has been monitoring the transition risks it faces by tracking its own greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption, and paper usage. The HKMA's climate objective is to achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions from Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 (air travel) across all areas of its operations by 2050 or earlier. As an interim emissions reduction target, the HKMA plans to achieve a complete elimination of Scope 1 emissions by converting all of its existing fleet to electric vehicles. With 2015 as the baseline year, the HKMA aims to reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% or more by 2030 or earlier, through a combination of carbon reduction and offsetting strategies. Despite challenges in quantifying Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will pursue a multi-pronged approach, to the extent feasible, to minimize greenhouse gas emissions from Scope 3 sources, such as paper consumption, waste generation, and air travel.
