The HKMA's long-term and near-term emission reduction targets have been formulated using the methodology of the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), which has been validated by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The HKMA has appointed the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency to verify the emissions, energy consumption, paper usage, and waste data disclosed in this report. The scope and basis of verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing its Annual Report 2022, the HKMA for the first time issued an independent Sustainable Development Report 2022. The HKMA's efforts to strengthen ESG reporting have been recognized, with the organization receiving the ESG Award in the Public Sector category at the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023." The HKMA is the first financial regulatory authority to receive an award in this category. The judging panel commended the HKMA for achieving high ESG standards. The Sustainability Report is clear and easy to read, while the appointment of an independent body to verify the methodology for target-setting and the environmental data disclosed in the report demonstrates the HKMA's commitment to transparent and accountable reporting. Furthermore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority was awarded the highest accolade in the "Non-Profit and Charitable Organization" category at the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "2023 Annual Report Awards." The jury commended the HKMA's annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial data and for effectively utilizing infographics, demonstrating the HKMA's commitment to enhancing financial literacy and promoting financial inclusion. To recognize the Monetary Authority's dedication to environmental stewardship, employee welfare, and the broader community, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has presented the "15+ Years of Caring Together" award to the Authority for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to effectively managing the environmental impact of its operations. Its internal Green Office Guidelines provide staff with guidance on resource utilization and the generation of office waste. The HKMA has integrated environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its owned and leased offices. When renovating offices, existing furniture and finishing materials will be reused as much as possible to minimize waste, and environmentally friendly building and decorative materials will be prioritized. The HKMA has continued to adopt this approach, thereby receiving LEED v7 Gold certification for its renovated office spaces in Two International Finance Centre in 2021, and BEAM Plus Interior Design Certification Level Gold in 2022. Through adopting new technologies and maximizing the use of existing technologies to enhance energy efficiency, this remains one of the key priorities of the Monetary Authority. In addition to promoting good practices such as turning off unnecessary lighting outside office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include the use of LED lighting, motion sensors, setting air-conditioning temperatures at appropriate levels, and optimizing energy use in IT network infrastructure. The HKMA's energy consumption continued to decline, reaching 2.59 MWh per person in 2023, a 29.7% decrease from the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Given the nature of the HKMA's day-to-day operations, its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions primarily arise from electricity consumption generated from fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined Scope 1 and Scope 2 emission intensity from purchased fuels and electricity amounted to 1.48 tCO₂e per capita, representing a 45.2% decrease compared to 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardised equipment, office software, and meeting facilities, the HKMA has adopted digital tools and technologies and streamlined its workflows through automation to build a digital working environment that enhances internal collaboration in online formats. 11. Paperless meetings have become the HKMA's primary mode of conducting meetings. To further reduce paper consumption and enhance efficiency, all internal administrative processes are primarily conducted electronically. Furthermore, the HKMA encourages staff to adopt green and digital working practices, replacing paper documents and communications with digital alternatives. Meanwhile, work is also underway to implement the electronic record-keeping system. The above green and digitalization measures have yielded positive results. In 2023, the use of paper by the HKMA amounted to 11.55 kilograms per person, a significant 64.8% reduction compared to 2015 (Figure 3). Following the COVID-19 pandemic, most international events have returned to in-person formats, and the development of Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre must be further promoted. Consequently, it is inevitable that staff of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will need to undertake official business overseas. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong encourages its staff, when participating in overseas activities, to take direct flights or combine multiple official trips whenever feasible. At the institutional level, the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO₂e in 2023 through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. Furthermore, the HKMA participates in the Gold Standard-verified carbon offset programme to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; the programme implements waste-to-energy, solar power, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue to implement similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA's procurement process takes sustainability and environmental factors into consideration. As part of a comprehensive review of institutional procurement policies and procedures, the current practice of procuring green products has been formalized into an official system, in compliance with the environmental specifications of the Government's Green Procurement List, particularly for electrical appliances and office consumables. Furthermore, the tender evaluation criteria have been updated to incorporate ESG factors and innovative proposals that enhance productivity and efficiency. At the same time, all suppliers must commit to complying with environmental regulations. Following the "4R" principles—Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle—the Hong Kong Monetary Authority adopted a three-pronged approach to minimize waste generation and manage waste disposal effectively. In addition, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to assist in developing targeted waste management strategies. Details of the non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various recyclable waste streams, are provided in the "Performance Summary" section on page 56. In 2023, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority participated for the first time in the red envelope recycling initiative organized by the management company of the International Finance Centre Office Tower. Employees returned approximately 3,000 used but still pristine red envelopes. These red envelopes were subsequently handed over to an environmental organization for distribution to the public for use during the upcoming Lunar New Year. Given that the HKMA's operational facilities and its standby data centre constitute the primary components of the institution's overall energy consumption, both data centres have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by the Green Building Council for existing data centres, thereby achieving an optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of 1.3. In 2023, the two data centers of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) received "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings, respectively, under the 2021 assessment guidelines titled "BEAM Plus Existing Buildings: Data Centers." The HKMA is the first and only institution in Hong Kong to have been awarded such ratings. Enhancing the energy efficiency of two data centers has long been a key focus of the Technical Group. To this end, the team has adopted green design in the renovation works and implemented energy-efficient best practices to reduce PUE and achieve relevant targets, including 24-hour monitoring of data center environmental facilities and continuous optimization of air flow and temperature settings. As the Technical Group continued to improve energy efficiency in the data centre, the HKMA commissioned an external consultant in December 2021 to conduct a review, aiming to comprehensively assess the data centre's green performance and develop recommendations to further enhance overall operations. The study was completed in mid-2022. Shortly after the completion of the study, the HKMA also began preparing to qualify for the "Green Data Centre" certification under the BEAM Plus certification scheme. The certification process is comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the Technical Working Group implemented optimization measures in line with the recommendations of the consultant's report to enhance energy performance and improve health-related aspects of the working environment within data centers.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency has independently verified the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (the "HKMA") 2023 environmental data ("2023 Data"). 2023 data include total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, greenhouse gas emissions from business aviation travel, paper consumption, and non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste and recyclable waste sent to landfills), along with their respective intensities and changes relative to 2015 levels. In addition, the 2023 figures include the amount of food waste generated during that year, its intensity, and the change compared to the levels at the time the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong launched its food waste recycling scheme in November 2022. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's greenhouse gas emission data are compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHG Protocol), jointly issued by the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD). The scope of verification covers data from January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2023, as well as data from January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2015 used for annual performance comparison (excluding food waste quantities). The scope of verification covered a total of five office and warehouse assets: four offices located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Taikoo Place Phase I, and 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, and one warehouse at 5) Loke Sun Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the validation is to provide reasonable assurance as to the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Authority reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from five assets. This verification exercise was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements (ISAE) 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB). The verification procedures are designed to form an opinion and reach conclusions to provide a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process is conducted in accordance with the GHG Protocol requirements. The verification process tested data integrity and accuracy by tracing selected sample data back to its sources, and also reviewed the fundamental procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, conducting reliability tests. The verification process also included validating internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 data, and selecting representative data and information for cross-checking. The underlying raw data and supporting evidence were also thoroughly reviewed during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for data collection and reporting. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Council's verification team was not involved in the 2023 data preparation process. Based on the results of this validation exercise, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Council has provided reasonable assurance for the 2023 data and concluded that the 2023 data are substantially accurate and reliable, and that the overall data collection mechanism of the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau is adequate. Shen Xiaoyin, Audit Supervisor, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Council, April 2024.

The threat posed by climate change is imminent, making accelerated global climate action an urgent imperative. The World Meteorological Organization confirmed that 2024 was the hottest year on record and marked the first time global average temperatures exceeded the critical 1.5°C threshold above pre-industrial levels. At the same time, although global greenhouse gas emissions eased slightly during the pandemic, they have recently reached record highs, highlighting the insufficiency of current climate change mitigation measures. In the effort to address global warming, climate-related risks are expected to intensify, with impacts on the economy and financial markets proving difficult to predict. Moreover, escalating geopolitical tensions, the increasing fragmentation of the global economic landscape, concerns over worsening energy security, and an uncertain economic outlook collectively pose greater challenges for countries in addressing climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Globally, the challenges of transition are most severe in Asia. As the World Economic Forum notes, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth but also the region most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. Therefore, Asia plays a pivotal role in whether the world can successfully achieve net-zero emissions targets. As Asia's leading international financial centre, Hong Kong has a duty to strengthen its leadership role and fully harness the power of finance to support and drive regional transformation. To this end, the HKMA announced the Sustainable Finance Action Plan last year, setting out our vision and roadmap for gradually integrating sustainable development principles into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses on two key objectives: enhancing the financial sector's capacity to manage climate-related risks, and assisting the industry in capitalizing on the emerging opportunities. At the same time, we lead by example and set the tone. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's sustainable development work encompasses four key areas: supporting the banking sector's transition to net zero, investing in a sustainable future, promoting net-zero financing, and advancing more inclusive sustainable development. The banking system plays a pivotal role in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and Asia, yet it faces significant risks in the course of this transition. Under the Action Plan, we have set ambitious targets requiring all banks to achieve net zero emissions from their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net zero emissions from their financed portfolio by 2050 or earlier. At the same time, we require all banks to enhance disclosure regarding climate-related risks and opportunities. While continuing to strengthen banks' climate risk management, we are also providing guidance on their transition planning to help them enhance their adaptive capacity and better manage related risks. We are also working with relevant stakeholders on preparatory efforts to align Hong Kong's sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, aiming to further enhance transparency in related activities across the industry. Additionally, we are refining the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Classification System, launched in May last year, to incorporate a broader range of sustainable activities, including transition activities. We aim to guide more capital towards sustainable and transition-related projects by providing clear guidelines. Climate change poses significant physical and transition risks that could affect the long-term financial performance and value of Exchange Fund investments. At the same time, it also presents opportunities for the Exchange Fund to achieve growth and exert a positive impact. Our experience demonstrates that investment returns and positive sustainability impacts can be aligned, with no inherent conflict between them. In light of this, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio by 2050 or earlier and have pledged in our Action Plan to support Asia's climate transition through the Fund's investments. Currently, the proportion of sustainable investments in portfolios has exceeded 10%. To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation last November, enabling joint investments to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition across Asia. Furthermore, we released the inaugural "HKMA ESG Expectations" document in September last year to further encourage fund managers to actively exercise ownership rights and adopt sound sustainable investment practices. Financial integration is particularly crucial for accelerating regional transformation. As an international financial hub and the preferred venue for arranging international sustainable bond issuances by Asian issuers (including provincial and municipal governments in the Mainland), Hong Kong plays a pivotal role in channeling capital to accelerate regional transformation. The Action Plan outlines the vision of developing Hong Kong into the region's preferred sustainable finance platform, as well as the objective of fostering sustainable finance innovation. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the Government's Sustainable Bond Programme to drive green bond innovation—including the issuance last February of the world's first multi-currency digital bonds—to expanding the scope of the Green and Sustainable Finance Funding Scheme to cover transition finance instruments in May last year, and to launching the Digital Bond Funding Scheme in November last year, we have been committed to encouraging issuers in the region to utilise Hong Kong's financial platform to raise the capital needed for carbon reduction and transition. To achieve a robust transition, beyond capital and innovation, a sustainable system that is inclusive and accessible is also required for support. This includes reliable sustainability data, high-quality information disclosure, and industry professionals with relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, we commit in our Action Plan to support the advancement of high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosure, and to address the regional shortfall in talent and knowledge for sustainable finance. We have made significant progress in supporting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainable disclosure, particularly by providing user-friendly climate disclosure templates to promote sustainability reporting among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). We also launched the "Green and Sustainable Finance" professional-level module under the Banking Professional Qualification Framework last November to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. Furthermore, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held last February and other related events, we have engaged stakeholders in discussions on sustainable development, thereby fostering collaboration and innovation. Within the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring that our operations align with a sustainable development vision. In our Action Plan, we committed to achieving net zero emissions across our own operations by 2030, advancing our original target by 20 years. In addition, we are actively preparing in accordance with the Government's roadmap to meet international sustainability disclosure standards. We began adopting electric vehicles in 2024 and incorporated low carbon emissions as a selection criterion during our procurement process. At the same time, we continue to enhance operational efficiency through digitalisation, foster a culture of sustainable development within the organisation, and motivate employees to actively engage in sustainability initiatives. Multilateral cooperation has long been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change; however, the restructuring of the international order and dramatic shifts in the geopolitical landscape have introduced new uncertainties into global climate action. However, climate change is an indisputable fact and is progressively intensifying. In addressing climate change, the current situation leaves us no room for complacency. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risk on Hong Kong's financial system, while also creating opportunities along the way. Entering 2025, we will continue to forge ahead with determination, vigorously advance our sustainability initiatives, and deepen our partnerships with like-minded collaborators. Despite facing significant challenges, we remain committed to supporting Hong Kong, Asia, and other regions in building a sustainable future.

Climate change is a major challenge facing today's generation. As an international financial centre and a sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development across Asia and the world. In October 2024, the HKMA unveiled its "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the Action Plan), setting out its vision in this field, including our future direction, the timelines for achieving key objectives, and how we expect the industry to collaborate with us to advance these efforts. The HKMA plans to consolidate Hong Kong's financial sector's and its own capacity to address climate-related risks, and to promote Asia's transition to a more sustainable economy, by formulating strategic policies, strengthening supervisory linkages, and enhancing internal operations. Through active engagement in international and regional dialogues, the HKMA is also committed to exerting influence in shaping green and sustainable finance policies and standards at both regional and global levels. As the banking regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the banking sector's climate resilience and supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness as they transition toward net zero emissions. Our key priorities for 2025 include: launching a new round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management practices and conducting the third round of consultation meetings to assess banks' implementation of the HKMA's relevant regulatory requirements and further strengthen their climate risk management capabilities; enhancing the integration of climate risk stress testing into the HKMA's regulator-led stress testing framework; continuing to advance the incorporation of climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review processes; preparing relevant regulatory provisions for the implementation by local banks of the Third Pillar disclosure framework on climate-related financial risks to be issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the International Sustainability Reporting Standards (ISSB Standards); completing the preparation of a new chapter, GS-2, in the Supervisory Policy Manual to provide guidance to banks on transition planning; and sharing best practices with the industry on climate risk management and the application of green fintech. In addition to its role as a banking regulator, the HKMA also serves as a catalyst, committed to fostering the development of a green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in providing financing for the transition. We have launched Phase 1 of the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Classification System, providing the industry with a tool to identify green and sustainable economic activities and to facilitate related capital mobilization. The Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAHK) has initiated the second phase of work on the classification taxonomy to expand its scope, incorporating transition elements, increasing the coverage of green economic activities, and integrating objectives related to climate change adaptation. Furthermore, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will organize another Green Fintech event in 2025 to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks. Hong Kong is well-positioned to meet the region's sustainable financing needs. To consolidate this role, we will continue to assist the government in implementing the "Sustainable Government Bonds Initiative," whose expanded scope will now include sustainable projects such as social responsibility projects. This move will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond markets and set a benchmark for other potential issuers in the region. Furthermore, we will continue to provide subsidies through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme to encourage more borrowers in the region to leverage Hong Kong's financing platforms to raise sustainable capital. We will also enhance our promotion efforts to encourage more mainland and other regional governments, institutions, and enterprises to raise green financing in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyze and support sustainable finance innovation, including providing funding to prospective issuers of digital green bonds through the Digital Green Bond Grant Scheme. While the demand from institutions and enterprises for high-quality sustainability disclosures is growing, entities vary in their capacity and readiness to provide such disclosures, and some may require additional guidance and support. In light of this, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with other members of the Cross-Sectoral Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance to make sustainable disclosure more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with more comprehensive climate disclosure tools, including user-friendly sustainable disclosure templates and supporting instruments; explore how technology can further enhance the accessibility and usability of existing resources; and collaborate with major local industry organizations to deliver training that meets sector needs. The sustainable finance market is dynamic and evolving, necessitating an expansion of the local talent pool and the filling of knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and the broader region. In 2025, the HKMA's key work includes collaborating with the banking industry to develop professional-level training modules on "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework," and identifying areas requiring further industry training through the upcoming "Future Banking Talent 2026–2030" study. Furthermore, we plan to collaborate with key stakeholders to enhance the promotion of the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme" and to review its scope of application. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation (IFC) through the Green Banking Alliance to launch targeted initiatives across Asia. These include conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering tailored skills enhancement and training support, fostering community engagement, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and delivering practical guidance to help banks develop roadmaps for integrating green finance as a core business function. As a responsible investor, the Monetary Authority has committed to achieving net zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio by 2050, in support of the broader economic transition. We will continuously enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund's investments through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, with a primary focus on the long-term resilience of the portfolio, while also exploring investment opportunities that can deliver positive climate outcomes. The Monetary Authority of Hong Kong is committed to setting an example in institutional sustainable development. In line with the timeline announced in the "Action Plan" to accelerate the commitment to net zero, the HKMA will pragmatically and progressively integrate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment, and reporting, continuing to promote the sustainable development of institutions. Specifically, we will conduct a double materiality assessment in 2025 to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring our focus remains on material topics. Furthermore, we will conduct energy audits and leverage technology-based solutions to assess the material impact of climate risks on our offices and operations, thereby enhancing our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap released by the Government and are actively preparing to make disclosures in accordance with ISSB standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment to selecting data centres for planned upgrade projects in accordance with the principles of energy efficiency and energy conservation. We will also expand our digital initiatives to promote sustainability and enhance efficiency, including the development of digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, while improving the overall digital experience for our employees, the banking sector, and the general public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. Through its multiple roles as a central banking authority, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainable development institution, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong has contributed to advancing and accelerating Hong Kong's, and indeed the entire Asia region's, transition to net-zero emissions. The HKMA has established a robust governance framework for sustainable development, which guides the formulation of relevant strategies and policies, oversees the implementation of related measures, and ensures that the HKMA's own operations and working methods integrate sustainability considerations. To advance sound corporate governance, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong has established a robust sustainability governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency for its sustainability-related initiatives. The governance framework ensures that the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes effectively incorporate sustainability factors, and establishes robust mechanisms to monitor and evaluate the progress and effectiveness of sustainability initiatives. The HKMA's sustainable development governance framework comprises: - The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which oversee the HKMA's work, including its efforts in sustainable development, and provide recommendations; - The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, which leads the HKMA's overall environmental, social, and governance (ESG) strategy and policy at the management level; - In the area of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related activities within the Investment Office; and - For other functional areas, relevant working groups are tasked with planning and implementing sustainable development measures related to banking and market development, as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sector level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Coordinating Group (the Coordinating Group), jointly established by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other relevant parties to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion of the HKMA's scope of sustainable development work over the past years, we established a Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainable development initiatives across the HKMA's various functional areas. - Provide guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans concerning ESG-related matters across the four functional areas of the banking sector, the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations;  - Oversee the implementation of ESG-related initiatives by the HKMA's various functional divisions;  - Evaluate the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and  - Supervise external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as ex officio members. Additionally, we will invite Assistant Executive Directors from key functions related to green and sustainable development to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on their major achievements and future plans. The Steering Committee holds regular meetings, supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Department, Corporate and Operations Division, External Affairs Division, and the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund. In addition to formulating and implementing their own sustainable development initiatives, the HKMA and the SFC jointly established a Steering Committee in May 2020. The Steering Group, as a cross-agency platform, provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sector efforts within the financial industry to address climate and environmental risks, thereby consolidating Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For further details on the Working Group's work, please refer to the chapter titled "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem."

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to enhancing the resilience of Hong Kong's financial system to climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong's climate objectives and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face a range of sustainability and climate-related impacts in their daily operations and must therefore proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play a pivotal role in the financial system by channeling capital toward green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the HKMA has particularly focused on strengthening banks' capacity to respond to and manage climate risks, while accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. In October, the Monetary Authority announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("the Action Plan"), setting out its vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional sustainable finance centre and support sustainable development across Asia and the globe. The Action Plan encompasses eight goals across four key areas. To assist the industry in achieving the relevant objectives of banking policies, we have been carrying out the following work. All banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions from their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero emissions from their financed portfolios by 2050 or earlier. All banks are also enhancing transparency on climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices on transition planning with the industry and launched a consultation on the draft of Chapter GS-2 "Transition Planning" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks' capacity to navigate the net-zero transition and manage associated risks. In addition, we are reviewing the supervisory review procedures used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy levels and to determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements. The objective is to incorporate factors identified by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) for the effective management of climate-related financial risks into the assessment process, and to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks—including transition planning—to address climate risks. The HKMA has been committed to aligning local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) standards and the Basel Committee's Third Pillar disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analyzing the latest developments in sustainability disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of ISSB standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the Action Plan. In May, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) published the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Classification System (the Classification System) to address industry concerns about greenwashing and to help channel capital toward green and sustainable activities. The classification framework covers 12 economic activities across four industries, aiming to align with the Common Taxonomy, as well as the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while also incorporating elements tailored to local circumstances. We have launched the second phase of our work to expand the scope of the Classification Catalogue and are consulting a broad range of stakeholders to further promote the mobilization of green and sustainable capital. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its regulatory oversight of banks' climate risk management and continued to support banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities, as well as to respond to climate change. The HKMA has also completed all work under the two-year plan formulated in 2022 to incorporate climate risk into the banking regulatory framework. To enhance banks' capacity to manage climate risks, the HKMA shared best practices observed during thematic reviews and consultation meetings with the banking sector. These primarily include: establishing a robust governance framework that clearly defines the responsibilities of the board of directors and senior management; and ensuring effective oversight of key areas related to climate-related risks, namely: (1) promoting and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) adopting appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) fostering a sound climate risk culture within the institution. The HKMA hosted a Balanced Regulatory Roundtable in August focused on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and participants from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority exchanged views on various climate risk-related topics, including the challenges banks face in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning, and finance. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and contributed to the HKMA's work on climate risk regulation and related areas. The HKMA launched a thematic review of banks' climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy in line with the supervisory expectations set out in Chapter GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The thematic review covers the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control, and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA held the second round of consultation meetings to assess the progress made by a new batch of banks in implementing Unit GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual, and to understand the challenges they face. The consultation meeting also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in the climate-related field, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and the issue of greenwashing. We provide feedback and guidance tailored to each bank's specific circumstances to support its climate risk management efforts. The HKMA completed the second round of the Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST) for the banking sector in 2024, involving 21 retail banks and 25 Hong Kong branches of international banking groups. Results show that across various scenarios—including those assuming the simultaneous occurrence of climate risks and macroeconomic downturns—the Hong Kong banking sector continues to demonstrate strong resilience in withstanding severe climate-related shocks. Compared with the CRST pilot scheme, participating banks have significantly enhanced their capacity to measure and assess climate risks. A report outlining the CRST findings and the good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025. The HKMA recognizes the numerous challenges banks face regarding data and methodologies in climate risk management and has therefore been committed to various initiatives to promote the application of technology in addressing these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessment, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) launched a Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to evaluate the potential impacts of physical risks on Hong Kong's residential and commercial buildings under various climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform by incorporating user feedback and adding more local data. Furthermore, the HKMA collaborates with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the broader financial services sector. During the year, we published an application practice guide and two white papers on compliance technology use cases (in English), outlining technology solutions for environmental, social and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as for managing greenwashing risks. We also hosted the third "FiNETech" forum, bringing together over 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore cooperation in green fintech. The Monetary Authority recognizes that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system; accordingly, it has expanded the scope of climate-related factors and scenarios incorporated into financial risk analysis and research to strengthen current monitoring efforts. In its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, the HKMA takes climate change into account and incorporates analyses of climate-related risks into its various financial stability reports. By actively participating in the Scenario Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has helped further enrich climate scenarios, thereby assisting central banks and regulators in understanding the impacts of climate change on the macroeconomy and the financial system. In November, the NGFS released the fifth edition of its long-term climate macro-financial scenarios to inform forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Transition Planning Task Force under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participated in analysing the interplay between transition planning by financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA has issued the "Practical Guidance on Banks' Adoption of Green Technology" (English version) to provide financial institutions with best practices for leveraging green technology and to support their transition to net zero. In terms of research, the HKMA undertook several applied research projects to examine the impact of climate change on the financial sector and the broader economy. Research topics include the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in buffering monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on the direction of foreign direct investment, and the role of the financial sector in the transition to a low-carbon economy. These research findings not only deepen our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability but also offer valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, aiding in the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, these studies will help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. Research findings are also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through various channels, including international forums and the "HKMA Research Memoranda." The Hong Kong Monetary and Financial Research Centre (the Centre), under the Hong Kong Institute of Finance, has published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provides evidence that low-emission enterprises can derive significant benefits from carbon pricing, highlighting its role in enhancing efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission enterprises. The study, published in the Centre's "Insights from Monetary Research," was shared with local and international scholars and policy researchers. The HKMA's Liquidity Arrangement Framework is a secured contingent funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. Under this framework, the HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations when assessing eligible collateral. The HKMA has actively engaged in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and promoting sustainable finance as a mainstream agenda. Through this engagement, we contribute to enhancing policy dialogue on climate change and its implications for financial stability at both international and regional levels, while drawing on these insights to strengthen Hong Kong's financial system's capacity to respond to climate-related challenges.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading hub for green and sustainable finance in the region, the Monetary Authority is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and catalysts, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As outlined in the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), the HKMA is committed to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by advancing net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to positioning Hong Kong as the preferred platform for sustainable financing for borrowers both within the region and globally; supporting technological innovation in the green segment of financial markets; enhancing sustainability disclosure across the industry; expanding the local pool of green finance talent; and addressing knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the broader region. To establish Hong Kong as the premier sustainable financing platform in the region and globally, catalyze sustainable finance innovation, support high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure, and address the regional talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance, the Government launched the Green Bond Financing Programme in 2018. This initiative demonstrates the Government's commitment to addressing climate change, advancing green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing approximately USD 28 billion worth of green bonds, sold to both institutional and retail investors. The proceeds have been allocated to more than 110 government green projects, including green buildings, waste management and recycling, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. We seize every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors, and distribution channels, thereby laying a solid foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the impact of the programme and further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a hub for green and sustainable finance, its scope was expanded to include sustainable projects, and it was renamed the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" (the Sustainable Bond Programme). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the sustainable bond framework, the government publishes an annual Green Bond Report detailing the allocation of proceeds raised from green bonds and their expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing approximately USD 3 billion worth of institutional green bonds under the Sustainable Bond Initiative. This issuance of trilateral-currency bonds covered bonds of various tenors denominated in Renminbi, US dollars, and euros. The bond issuance attracted participation from diverse categories of investors, with strong subscription demand resulting in total subscriptions exceeding USD 15 billion in value. The 20-year and 30-year RMB green bonds mark the government's inaugural issuance of such instruments, representing the longest tenor RMB bonds issued by the government to date. They provide a new benchmark for the market and further enhance the demonstrative role of the Sustainable Bond Initiative. These bonds have further diversified the range of offshore renminbi investment products available in Hong Kong. Furthermore, the robust response from global investors to the green bonds issued by the Government underscores their endorsement of Hong Kong's commitment to advancing green and sustainable development. To encourage more regional borrowers to tap Hong Kong's financing platform for raising sustainable development funds, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to implement the Green and Sustainable Finance Subsidy Scheme, which was launched in May 2021, providing subsidies for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The programme has been widely embraced by the industry. As of the end of 2024, it has provided funding for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total value exceeding US$140 billion. The scheme was extended by three years in May 2024 to 2027, and its scope of financial support was expanded to include transition bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the initiative is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries within the region to leverage Hong Kong's transition finance platform to progressively reduce their carbon emissions. - Approved subsidies for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total volume exceeding US$140 billion (as of end-2024); extended the programme by three years to 2027 and expanded the scope of subsidisation to include transition financing instruments. Meanwhile, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has actively promoted Hong Kong's sustainable finance platform, achieving exemplary results. In August, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued its fourth offshore local government bond in Hong Kong, totaling RMB 7 billion, comprising RMB 2.7 billion in green bonds, RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds, and RMB 0.9 billion in social responsibility bonds. In September, the People's Government of Guangdong Province issued its inaugural offshore bonds in Hong Kong, totaling RMB 5 billion, including RMB 1.5 billion in green bonds. In October, the People's Government of Hainan Province also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, with a total amount of RMB 3 billion, comprising RMB 1 billion in blue bonds and RMB 1 billion in sustainability bonds. These bond issuance activities have repeatedly highlighted Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating green and sustainable capital flows between the Mainland and the rest of the world. Through the above measures, Hong Kong has consolidated its position as the preferred platform for sustainable financing in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association (ICMA), in 2024, Hong Kong continued to be the leading hub in Asia for arranging the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds, with a total volume of USD 43.1 billion arranged through Hong Kong, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyse innovation in sustainable finance, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two landmark tranches of tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024: the world's first tokenised government green bonds, and the world's first multi-currency digital bonds. The issuance demonstrates the Government's support for market participants in the region to apply asset digitization and innovative technologies in the fields of green and sustainable finance. In November, the HKMA launched the Digital Bond Funding Scheme to promote digital bond issuance in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting innovation in the local green and sustainable finance market. The Working Group on Sustainable Disclosure, established under the Cross-Industry Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance (CSG), has been actively working towards the adoption of the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) standards in Hong Kong. The Government issued the Hong Kong Sustainability Disclosure Roadmap in December 2024, setting out a clear pathway for large public-interest entities to fully adopt IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards by no later than 2028. The HKMA has maintained close cooperation with local and international partners to support entities at various stages of readiness in achieving high-quality sustainability disclosure, thereby making sustainability disclosure more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continue to encourage the Steering Committee's adoption of the "Non-Listed Company Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire" (the Questionnaire), which was launched in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The questionnaire provides user-friendly disclosure templates, facilitating sustainable reporting by enterprises, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The questionnaire was launched in an electronic version in February 2024 to facilitate online submission by enterprises (see QR code below). The HKMA is refining the questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to enhance its usability. Specific measures include identifying core questions within the questionnaire and providing common usage scenarios. In addition, we also strive to enhance the compatibility of the questionnaire with other supporting tools on the Steering Group's website. For more information on the questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. The HKMA leads by example by making high-quality sustainability disclosures in its Sustainability Report, in line with the latest global standards, to demonstrate its commitment. The report contains rich content on the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's institution-level operational risks related to climate change, as well as plans and progress in implementing measures to achieve climate goals. For further details on the sustainability disclosures relating to our own operations, please refer to the chapter titled "Sustainability at the HKMA". Given the rapid evolution of the sustainable finance market, the HKMA is enhancing skills training within the banking sector and fostering knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders to address gaps in expertise and talent. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking professionals in sustainable finance, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) partnered with the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB) to launch the foundational level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit under the Banking Competency Framework in July 2023. This module aims to assist professionals in the banking industry in acquiring knowledge of green and sustainable finance more effectively and in developing relevant professional competencies. It covers four key areas: (1) green and sustainable finance products and services; (2) sustainable/climate risk management; (3) sustainability disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainable strategy, compliance, and governance. Furthermore, the professional-level module on "Green and Sustainable Finance" targeting senior and middle-level banking practitioners was also launched in November. To equip bank practitioners with the necessary training, the Hong Kong Association of Banks (HKAB), as the managing body for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, launched the foundational-level training course for the module in May. Following the launch of the Professional Level in November, the HKMA will collaborate with the banking industry in 2025 to develop professional-level training programmes. To better understand the future skill and training needs of the banking sector, the HKMA is currently collaborating with the banking industry on a study titled "Future Banking Talent 2026–2030," with the aim of publishing the findings in 2025. This joint study follows the June 2020 publication of "Future Banking Talent 2021–2025". The findings of the follow-up research will provide important reference for the industry, assisting in the formulation and adjustment of talent training strategies and measures to support the sustainable development of the banking sector. The HKMA, in collaboration with the Steering Group, continues to support the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme," which provides funding for practitioners, graduates, and students to undertake training related to sustainable finance. As of December 2024, a total of 85 international and local courses were registered as eligible training courses under the scheme, with more than 5,700 reimbursement applications approved. The Government announced in the 2025-26 Budget that the scheme will be extended to 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international cooperation. As a founding member of the Capacity Alliance for Sustainable Investment (CASI), the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Promotion Office co-hosted a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, focusing on global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks, and innovative tools. Furthermore, the Monetary Authority supports the establishment of the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) Hong Kong office in October and will leverage GFANZ's network and expertise to enhance capacity-building and training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a significant global asset owner and manager, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that strong financial performance and positive impact can reinforce each other, the HKMA upholds responsible investment principles in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritizing sustainable assets and requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise ownership rights. The HKMA adopts a prudent investment approach under the principle of "preserving capital first, achieving long-term growth," and believes that fully incorporating environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors can help mitigate investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a steadfast signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is committed to advancing its responsible investment agenda. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the urgent issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and seeking improved risk-adjusted long-term returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring a range of investment instruments to channel capital toward sustainable investments across diverse asset classes (Figure 1). The HKMA, in its capacity as a major investor, contributes to advancing the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA released the "HKMA Expectations on ESG" and made the document available to its investment partners through annual ESG workshops and the HKMA website. We collaborate with like-minded investors, regulators, and international organizations to establish industry operating standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial sector and central banking community. Through these collaborative efforts, we are committed to fostering a future where finance and sustainable development advance hand in hand. In October, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) unveiled its "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), outlining its commitment to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 or earlier through the Investment Portfolio of the Exchange Fund, and to mobilize partners in support of the transition to a low-carbon economy, thereby further solidifying its dedication to investing in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, has established a responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the management of the Exchange Fund's investments. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA's approach to practising responsible investment while concurrently safeguarding the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive Officer of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks associated with Exchange Fund investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the Responsible Investment Framework and risk management guidelines and monitors their implementation through regular reports from the Sustainable Investment Group of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office is chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer and is responsible for coordinating and monitoring all ESG-related activities of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. The motions and progress reports discussed by the ESG Committee at its quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Furthermore, the Green and Sustainable Oversight Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAHK) and attended by the Chief Executive and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, holds regular meetings to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across various functions of the MAHK, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in order to implement the MAHK's overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Group works closely with different teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) to integrate ESG factors and assists EFIO senior management in overseeing ESG-related, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across various investment portfolios:  - Public market investments: The Credit, Regulatory and Monitoring Committee, composed of EFIO senior staff, reviews the incorporation of ESG factors into credit risk models based on the Sustainable Investment Group's input, and monitors the ESG status of fixed-income portfolios through regular reporting from the Risk Management and Surveillance Department. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Team has also participated in the selection, appointment, and monitoring process of external equity portfolio managers from an ESG perspective (for details, see the section "Promoting Active Stewardship" under "Risk Management" on page 39). Private market investments – the Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the Monetary Authority, will consider ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams for each investment proposal. The Monetary Authority understands that the physical and transition risks posed by climate change, as well as the associated opportunities, may affect the long-term financial performance of Exchange Fund investment portfolios. The United Nations Environment Programme's Emissions Gap Report 2024 projects that, without a global-scale mobilization to rapidly cut greenhouse gas emissions, global average temperatures will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Uncertainties surrounding policy shifts, technological advancements, and behavioral changes in response to rising temperatures could exacerbate transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuations. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also pose additional risks of physical damage and financial losses to investment projects. Amid these challenges, governments and industries worldwide are turning toward sustainable solutions, creating potentially attractive long-term investment opportunities in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies, and sustainable infrastructure. The Monetary Authority of Hong Kong believes that investing in a sustainable future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund; accordingly, it places particular emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG considerations. The Monetary Authority has set a target for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio to reach net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, and is advancing this goal through an orderly, three-pronged approach (see Figure 3). In 2024, the Monetary Authority announced its Action Plan, which reinforced the Exchange Fund's commitments and efforts related to climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the Monetary Authority has taken the approach of proactively engaging rather than excluding or divesting from investable projects. Investing in a Sustainable Future: The Exchange Fund's Portfolio Aims to Achieve Net Zero Emissions by 2050. This includes actively expanding the scope and variety of sustainable investments, particularly climate transition-themed investments in both public and private markets. ESG factors will be integrated into every investment decision, with particular emphasis on climate change and transition prospects. Clear ESG expectations aligned with international standards and best practices will be established and required of all external investment managers, investee companies, and counterparties. The Fund is committed to reducing the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of its equity portfolio by 67% from 2017 levels by 2030. Through investment, the Fund will support regional transitions, continue engaging with external investment managers to optimize transition-enabling opportunities, and actively identify and prioritize high-quality investment opportunities that foster Asia's transition while delivering positive global impacts. First, maintaining a diversified and robust portfolio is crucial to achieving the Exchange Fund's primary investment objective. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, with potential implications for investment returns and risk. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA is able to seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transformation that possess advanced technology and sound corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including those in high-emission sectors. Second, addressing climate change requires the transformation of core "brown" industries. Excluding relevant investment projects or engaging in divestment alone does not help address carbon emissions. In contrast, the HKMA has supported these sectors by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising its ownership rights, driving their transition to sustainable and low-carbon operational practices, thereby generating beneficial transformations for both itself and the global community. Net-zero investment strategies have evolved from a focus on green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, thereby driving comprehensive decarbonization across the entire economy. As a global asset owner, the HKMA understands that the long-term resilience of an asset portfolio depends not only on the portfolio's own adjustments but also on broader economic transformation. Although no single perfect solution exists, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority improved its responsible investment strategy in 2024, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive the transition while supporting the Exchange Fund and global net-zero objectives. This strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including the integration of ESG factors into fundamental analysis, stewardship, portfolio decarbonization tilts, and thematic investments in various asset classes aligned with pathways to net zero emissions. In the open market, this may involve tilting portfolios toward ESG leaders and providers of climate solutions, complemented by supervisory efforts to drive corporate transformation. In the private markets, greater emphasis may be placed on fostering investment projects that drive transformation. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the Monetary Authority continues to seek opportunities that facilitate climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's portfolio. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for more than 10% of the Exchange Fund's "investment portfolio," with financial performance broadly in line with the relevant asset class benchmarks (Figure 5). - Public market investments: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has launched an actively managed global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and has extended the application of a customized low-carbon stock index to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA continues to seek ways to fund sustainable projects while offering competitive returns on green, social, and sustainability (GSS) bonds (see the case study "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds"). Private Market Investment – The Monetary Authority is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio by capitalizing on investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA is also actively identifying and evaluating investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including by establishing strategic partnerships with international organizations (see the section "Joining Forces to Tackle Climate Challenges in Asia and Beyond"). - Passive portfolios benchmarked to ESG indices  - Customized decarbonization strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios not benchmarked to ESG indices  - Active portfolios focused on governance  - Active ESG portfolios centered on sustainability and climate transition  - Sustainable projects, such as renewable energy infrastructure and green-certified buildings and warehouses  - Funds focused on energy transition and decarbonization efforts globally, in Asia, and in the Global South  - Green, social, and sustainability bonds  - A green bond fund managed by an international organization  - The "Multilateral Credit Portfolio Partnership" (MCPP) program, managed by the International Finance Corporation and focused on sustainable projects in emerging markets  - The "MCPP One Planet" initiative, which provides climate-related investment funding for emerging markets aligned with the Paris Agreement  - The Monetary Authority of Singapore's investment in green bonds issued by a semi-official institution The funds raised through green bonds are allocated to multiple projects, including the upgrade of aging equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrade projects encompass the optimization of monitoring and control systems as well as pump performance, thereby generating positive environmental benefits through wastewater management, waste reduction, and recycling processes. In addition to continued wastewater and sludge treatment, these facilities compost or reuse dewatered sludge to produce fertilizers, charcoal, cement, and other building materials, achieving a sludge recovery rate of up to 100%. These facilities also utilize gases generated during the sludge treatment process to power boilers and generate electricity. The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a multilateral development bank. The bond is providing funding for multiple projects, including the restoration of a national canal system. As one of the country's largest irrigation systems, the canal is designed to divert excess river water to arid regions. The primary objective of the project is to repair the deteriorating canal linings to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water-use efficiency, and reclaim waterlogged areas. In addition, the project has also conducted skills training for local stakeholders to promote the adoption and effective utilization of modern irrigation technologies, such as micro-irrigation, and sustainable farming practices.

The Monetary Authority is committed to becoming a responsible and sustainable institution. One of the key priorities for the HKMA in 2024 to deliver on this commitment is to advance the target year for achieving net-zero emissions across its operations to 2030, 20 years earlier than originally planned, in alignment with the Sustainable Finance Action Plan. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the Monetary Authority has committed to advancing employee training and well-being, while striving to enhance financial inclusion and improve public financial literacy. The Green and Sustainable Finance Steering Committee (the Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive Officer of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, serves as the primary decision-making body for institutional sustainable finance initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA's commitment to addressing climate change, the Oversight Committee approved in October 2024 a new target for the HKMA to achieve net-zero emissions from its institutional operations by 2030 or earlier, as part of the Sustainable Finance Action Plan (the Plan). At the departmental level, the Assistant Commissioner for Institutional Development and Operations provides guidance on implementing sustainable development measures in institutional operations, employee well-being, and community engagement, and submits regular reports to the Steering Committee. The Administrative Group serves as the coordinator and central hub for the implementation, communication, and reporting of sustainable development initiatives. A green office task force comprising staff from various operational departments, along with a volunteer service team, provides an additional layer of support. The former serves as a platform for brainstorming and proposing ideas on how to create a green workplace, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of employee engagement in volunteer activities. To recognize the HKMA's dedication to environmental stewardship, employee well-being, and the broader community, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has presented the "15+ Years of Caring Together" award to the HKMA consecutively from 2006 to 2024, spanning 18 years. The HKMA's sustainable development strategy continues to adopt a framework built on three pillars: environmental stewardship, employee well-being, and social responsibility. Focusing on the HKMA's day-to-day operations in decarbonization and digitalization, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 or earlier; adopting green procurement requirements in line with government guidelines; promoting more environmentally friendly operating practices across the financial sector and the wider community; building an engaged and talented workforce to achieve the HKMA's strategic objectives; fostering a collaborative, caring, and inclusive work environment that values diversity and strengthens employees' sense of belonging; providing a high-quality workplace that supports healthy lifestyles; cultivating a culture of social responsibility; integrating social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management; and advancing financial inclusion while enhancing public financial literacy through consumer education initiatives. The HKMA is committed to addressing climate change and leading by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced that it would advance its target for achieving net-zero emissions in its own operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of its original commitment, as part of the Action Plan. The Monetary Authority has revised its roadmap towards net-zero transition, focusing on responsibly managing the environmental impact of daily operations. Key priorities include reducing carbon emissions, enhancing energy efficiency, cutting paper usage, and promoting waste recycling, while fully leveraging improvements made by local power companies in their generation fuel mix. Furthermore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has established a digitalised working environment to enhance efficiency while simultaneously reducing its carbon footprint. Furthermore, recognizing the importance of fostering a culture of sustainability, the Monetary Authority has been actively encouraging its staff to adopt sustainable practices through continuous promotional initiatives and events. Under the primary 2030 net-zero emissions target, the HKMA has been exploring the adoption of carbon-embedded tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and prioritise low-carbon procurement wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023, the HKMA has fully offset the carbon emissions associated with its air travel by purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in carbon offset programs. The HKMA will expand its carbon embedding and carbon offset schemes to cover all other major carbon emissions.
