In addition to the above-mentioned environmental commitments related to actual operations, the Monetary Authority continues to promote the market's low-carbon transition, ranging from the introduction of electronic document submission and processing procedures to encouraging electronic payments and the recycling of coins back into circulation. The remainder of this chapter details the strategies adopted by the Monetary Authority in leading environmental initiatives, as well as in promoting employee well-being and caring for society. Under the HKMA's overarching institutional risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing potential risks and threats arising from climate change that the HKMA faces in its day-to-day operations. To more effectively assess the potential impact of climate change on operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and examined both actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring business continuity, the HKMA has designed and implemented a range of measures at its offices to mitigate potential physical hazards, fires, and other emergencies. In addition, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans to incorporate comprehensive measures that cover not only offices but also communication and computer facilities. The HKMA regularly conducts evacuation and failover facility drills to ensure staff are always prepared to implement contingency measures. The HKMA has also been monitoring the transition risks it faces by tracking its own greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, waste generation, energy consumption, and paper usage. The HKMA's latest climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions from Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 emissions associated with its institutional operations by 2030 or earlier. These targets were established with reference to the methodology of the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi). The HKMA employs the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report institutional emissions. Scope 1 emissions refer to direct emissions from gasoline-powered vehicles. Given its operational nature, the HKMA's primary greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions stem from Scope 2 indirect emissions generated by the consumption of fossil fuels for electricity production. In the absence of data specific to individual suppliers, the HKMA adopted a conservative approach to estimate Scope 3 emissions associated with purchased goods (including capital goods) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste disposed of in landfills, as well as employee air travel and commuting. Detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024 are presented in the "Summary of Performance" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and criteria for the verification are set out in the accompanying "Verification Statement" at the end of this report. The HKMA leads by example, upholding the same climate-related standards that it expects the banks it supervises and the financial system it oversees to follow. As a first step toward green mobility, the Monetary Authority began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this initiative in 2025 to achieve comprehensive green mobility. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in the various renovation projects undertaken in 2024, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority reused existing furniture and interior finishes or exchanged old items for new ones at a discounted price, thereby reducing waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and conservation measures in its offices and data centers. As part of its 2024 data center facility upgrade, it adopted a modular uninterruptible power supply (UPS) system, further optimizing the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its Green Building Environmental Assessment (BEAM) certified data centers. This design offers flexible capacity expansion, improved operational efficiency under partial load, and incorporates advanced cooling technology with higher power density, contributing to reduced overall energy consumption. The HKMA has enhanced internal virtual collaboration through its Digital Workshop, complemented by streamlined workflows, effectively reducing paper consumption. Furthermore, drawing on manufacturers' software update cycles, the HKMA extended the service life of mobile and desktop devices, thereby extending their period of secure usage. To reduce office-generated waste, the Monetary Authority has adhered to the "4R" principles—refuse, reduce, reuse, and recycle—and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The HKMA has placed recycling bins at various convenient locations within its offices to collect different types of recyclable materials. To enhance recycling rates, the HKMA installed additional recycling bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit nets in 2024. Furthermore, since November 2022, the HKMA has been sending collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA joined the Environmental Protection Department's "Waste Reduction Pledge," committing to implement measures aimed at reducing waste generated from its various activities. The HKMA continues to prioritize procurement of goods that comply with the environmental specifications set out in the Government's "Green Procurement List," particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong encourages staff to carefully plan their itineraries, such as consolidating multiple trips when attending overseas events. At the institutional level, the HKMA has purchased sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing its annual business aviation travel carbon emissions by approximately 10%. Furthermore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) participated in a Gold Standard-certified carbon offset programme to offset the remaining carbon emissions from its air travel; the programme focuses on renewable energy generation and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA organized various learning activities for staff, including lectures and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance employees' understanding of environmental sustainability issues. The Monetary Authority of Hong Kong will hold its inaugural "Green Month" from Earth Day on 22 April throughout May 2024, with the theme "Green Thinking, Green Living, Green Working." This presents a valuable opportunity for the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to demonstrate its commitment and drive in advancing environmental sustainability within its own operational practices. The event included activities such as the "Sustainable Living BINGO Scorecard" to encourage employees to adopt green lifestyles, a "Save the Earth" quiz, and an indoor plant care workshop on Japanese-style kokedama; it also featured a presentation of waste audit results and an introduction to best practices in recycling by operators of community recycling centers. To sustain the momentum of "Green Month," the HKMA launched a recycling campaign in October lasting approximately six months, highlighting the responsible disposal of waste and reminding staff that small individual habit changes can significantly enhance the organization's overall recycling performance. A highlight of the event was the launch of the "Green Fit Action" video series, in which several senior executives shared practical recycling tips. The initiative also launched a series of screen savers, prominently designed posters, intranet articles, and electronic prompts to encourage staff to lead by example in waste reduction and increased recycling. In late 2024, the HKMA conducted an employee survey to gauge staff understanding of sustainability and to gather their views on proposed green office initiatives. The findings will assist in formulating future sustainability training programs and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong's central banking authority, the Monetary Authority regards itself as a key driver of change and is committed to leading the acceleration of the low-carbon transition, promoting sustainable practices across the financial sector and society at large. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has introduced a range of measures to enhance the efficiency of its external processes. Following the successful launch of the Shared Data Submission Platform in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform's scope in 2024 to include non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility operators, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data. The purpose of expanding the platform's service scope is to further streamline the submission process for reporting entities, provide all users with a more seamless experience, and reinforce the HKMA's commitment to sustainability. Other new measures introduced in 2024 include the SurveyTool, which enables banks to respond to HKMA questionnaire surveys through a streamlined submission process, and an intelligent information and document management system that provides users with a centralized platform offering advanced search capabilities and access to bank-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Authority (HKQAA) has conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (the "Data") provided by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The data include total energy consumption in 2024, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste and recyclable waste sent to landfills), and GHG emissions from air travel, along with their respective intensity ratios. In addition, the data also include Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions arising from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste and recyclable waste sent to landfills), and employee commuting for 2023 and 2024, along with their corresponding emission intensities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's greenhouse gas emission data are compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, jointly issued by the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD). The scope of verification covered a total of six office and warehouse assets: five offices located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Taikoo Place Phase I, 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre; and one warehouse at 6) Luen Shing Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of validation is to provide reasonable assurance of the accuracy and reliability of the data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Authority reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from six assets. This verification exercise was conducted in accordance with ISAE 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB). The verification procedures are designed to form an opinion and reach conclusions that provide a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process is conducted in accordance with the GHG Protocol requirements. The validation process tested data integrity and accuracy by tracing selected sample data back to their sources. It also reviewed the fundamental procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and conducted reliability tests. The verification process also includes validating internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for data preparation, and selecting representative data and information for verification. The relevant original data and supporting evidence were also thoroughly reviewed during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for data collection and reporting. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Council verification team has not participated in the data preparation process. Based on the findings of this validation exercise, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance over the data and concludes that: - the data are substantially accurate and reliable; - the Monetary Authority's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Reviewed by Samantha Sam, Chief Auditor, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Association, March 2025.
